methodological_rigor.justification: The study identifies epigenetically stable loci (ESLs) from 1658 young healthy individuals (age 18) and validates them across 8,886 individuals in 29 cohorts, covering hematological cancers (n=3159), cardiovascular disease (n=2788), and healthy controls (n=2939). Multi-platform validation (Illumina 450K/EPIC arrays, WGBS) strengthens the ESL definition. Statistical approaches are appropriate and well-described: Kaplan-Meier with log-rank test, multivariate Cox proportional hazards (adjusted for age, sex, and 12 immune cell types), Fisher's exact test for genomic enrichment, permutation tests for clonal matching, and Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons. Power analysis was conducted for the cardiogenic shock cohort. The longitudinal design (paired diagnosis-relapse samples in AML, CLL, BCP-ALL) with permutation testing provides strong evidence for clonal epigenetic memory. Main limitations include: (1) exclusive reliance on Illumina array data covering <2% of the genome with promoter bias; (2) the investigators were not blinded to allocation during outcome assessment; (3) the cardiovascular cohorts are retrospective with no direct mechanistic validation of ESL perturbation causing gene dysregulation.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The Framingham Heart Study arm (n=2281, up to 14 years follow-up) provides LoE 2b evidence for the association between DMI and cardiovascular outcomes, as it is a prospective cohort study with pre-specified covariates and relevant clinical endpoints (CVD, CHD, CHF, all-cause mortality). Hazard ratios for CVD (HR=1.30, p=0.018) and CHD (HR=1.57, p=0.011) remain significant after adjustment for age, sex, and immune cell fractions. The cardiogenic shock sub-cohort (n=64) independently validates DMI as a prognostic marker (HR=3.76, p=0.006), independent of clonal hematopoiesis status. The hematological malignancy data demonstrates clinical relevance by tracking leukemic burden during treatment and predicting impending relapse. The broad applicability to common conditions (aging, cardiovascular disease, leukemia) with a blood-based, cost-effective assay (methylation array) strengthens translational potential.

reporting_quality.justification: The Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary is referenced, consistent with high-quality standards for observational/biomarker studies. Statistical methods are thoroughly described in both the methods section and relevant results. Sample sizes, exclusion criteria, and cohort characteristics are clearly stated. The analysis is deliberately non-randomized and non-blinded for valid reasons (retrospective methylation analysis), explicitly acknowledged in the Statistics section. Source data are provided as a Source Data file, and publicly available GEO datasets are referenced with accession numbers (GSE40279, GSE87571, GSE115278, GSE197676, etc.). Limitations of the Infinium array technology (coverage, promoter bias) are transparently acknowledged in the Discussion. Power analysis was performed for the cardiogenic shock cohort. CpG exclusion criteria (SNP overlap, cross-reactivity, age-association) are explicitly detailed. Minor limitation: raw ESL methylation data from the novel cardiogenic shock EPIC array profiling is not deposited in a public repository.

novelty_literature.justification: The concept of DNA methylation outliers as biomarkers has precedents in breast and cervical cancer pre-neoplastic tissue studies (Teschendorff et al.), but this work makes a significant advance by: (1) defining a large, robust set of blood-specific ESLs (31,744 unmethylated loci) applicable pan-cancer and to non-cancer disease; (2) demonstrating epigenetic clonal memory across paired diagnosis-relapse samples in three distinct leukemia types using low-recurrence ESLs; (3) linking DMI to cardiovascular risk independent of and additive to known clonal hematopoiesis genetic drivers; (4) proposing a mechanistic framework connecting ESL perturbation to TF binding motif disruption and age-associated gene silencing. The integration across hematological malignancies, aging, and cardiovascular disease under a unified epigenetic instability framework is genuinely novel and clinically impactful.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-organized, progressing logically from ESL identification, to cancer validation, to aging association, to cardiovascular outcome analysis, to mechanistic exploration. The multi-cohort design is clearly explained. Figures are appropriately designed for the data types presented (UMAP, boxplots, Kaplan-Meier curves, volcano plots). Statistical notations and CIs are consistently reported. Methods are detailed and technically reproducible. The Discussion appropriately acknowledges limitations (array coverage, lack of causal mechanistic proof, retrospective design). Minor issues include some density in the Methods section requiring methodological expertise to parse, and the mechanistic section (TF motif overlap) could benefit from stronger functional validation to support the proposed models.

key_strengths: Robust ESL definition from 1658 young healthy individuals validated across 8,886 subjects in 29 cohorts spanning hematological malignancies and cardiovascular disease
Clonal epigenetic memory demonstrated by permutation-validated paired diagnosis-relapse matching in AML (9/15), CLL (31/40), and BCP-ALL (24/24) using low-recurrence ESLs
DMI independently predicts cardiovascular outcomes in Framingham Heart Study (HR=1.57 for CHD, p=0.011) after adjustment for age, sex, and 12 immune cell types
DMI serves as a complement to genetic clonal hematopoiesis markers—predicts survival in cardiogenic shock independently of DNMT3A/TET2 mutations (HR=3.76, p=0.006)
Mechanistic framework linking ESL perturbations to TF binding motif disruption (SP, KLF, AP-2 families) and age-associated gene silencing supported by integrated methylation-expression-chromatin data
key_concerns: Exclusive reliance on Illumina array data covering <2% of the genome with promoter bias limits discovery of intergenic regulatory ESLs that may be clinically important
Investigators were not blinded to allocation during outcome assessment, acknowledged in Methods but potential source of ascertainment bias in outcome classification
The mechanistic link between ESL perturbation and gene dysregulation is correlative; no direct functional experiments (e.g., targeted demethylation, TF binding assays) establish causation

The cardiogenic shock validation cohort (n=64) was deliberately underpowered relative to the original clonal hematopoiesis study, limiting conclusions about the relative contribution of DMI versus genetic CH
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a high-quality multi-cohort biomarker study with robust statistical methodology, meaningful clinical associations in cardiovascular and hematological disease, and a novel integrated framework linking epigenetic instability to clonal hematopoiesis and aging; the correlative mechanistic evidence and array-based genome coverage are limitations appropriate for minor revisions at a tier-1 translational journal.
